questions.explanation: B is correct. SAGACIOUS = having or showing keen mental discernment and good judgement; wise. Its antonym = OBTUSE (slow to understand; lacking sharpness of mind; dull). Prudent, perceptive, and judicious are all SYNONYMS of sagacious (all imply wisdom or good judgement). OBTUSE is the only antonym here, meaning mentally slow or stupid.

C is correct. OBDURATE = stubbornly refusing to change one's opinion or course of action. Synonyms: stubborn, intransigent, unyielding, inflexible, recalcitrant. 'Flexible' and 'agreeable' are antonyms. 'Compassionate' is unrelated — obdurate has no connection to compassion (though an obdurate person might also be uncompassionate, they are different concepts). Trap: 'Flexible' = direct antonym.

C is correct. LOQUACIOUS = tending to talk a great deal; talkative. Antonym = TACITURN = reserved or uncommunicative in speech; saying little. Garrulous and voluble are SYNONYMS of loquacious (all mean talkative). Verbose = using too many words (also a synonym of loquacious). Trap: All other options mean 'talkative' in various degrees — only taciturn means 'quiet/reserved'.

B is correct. ACRIMONY = bitterness or ill feeling, especially in speech or manner. Synonyms: bitterness, rancour, hostility, asperity. 'The negotiations ended in acrimony' = they ended bitterly. Antonyms: harmony, goodwill, cordiality. Trap: Harmony and sweetness are antonyms; generosity is unrelated.

D is correct. MUNIFICENT = larger or more generous than is usual or necessary; very generous. Antonym = NIGGARDLY = ungenerous with money; stingy; miserly. Generous, lavish, and bountiful are all SYNONYMS of munificent. NIGGARDLY is the only antonym in the list. Trap: 'Generous' appears to be the opposite of what many expect, but it is a synonym; the antonym is niggardly/miserly.

B is correct. EBULLIENT = cheerful and full of energy; exuberant. Synonyms: exuberant, buoyant, effervescent, vivacious. Antonyms: subdued, melancholic, depressed. 'Her ebullient personality lifted everyone's spirits' = her exuberant, energetic personality. Trap: Depressed, subdued, melancholic are all antonyms of ebullient — they describe the opposite of high energy and cheerfulness.

C is correct. PAUCITY = the presence of something in only small or insufficient quantities; scarcity. Antonym = ABUNDANCE (a very large quantity of something). Scarcity, dearth, and deficiency are all SYNONYMS of paucity. Only ABUNDANCE is the antonym. Trap: All three wrong options (scarcity, dearth, deficiency) mean 'shortage' — same as paucity; only abundance means 'plenty'.

C is correct. OSTENSIBLE = stated or appearing to be true, but not necessarily so; apparent (often used to suggest the stated reason is not the real one). 'The ostensible reason for the visit was to inspect the building, but the real purpose was a negotiation.' Synonyms: apparent, professed, supposed, seeming. Antonyms: genuine, authentic, real. Trap: Genuine and authentic are antonyms (they mean truly what they appear to be, not merely seemingly so); hidden = not a synonym (ostensible = visible/stated, not hidden).

C is correct. INTREPID = fearless; adventurous (often the heading of Explorer/adventurer stories). Antonym = PUSILLANIMOUS = showing a lack of courage or determination; timid; faint-hearted. Brave, audacious, and valiant are all SYNONYMS of intrepid. PUSILLANIMOUS is a high-frequency SSC word meaning 'cowardly in a petty way'. Trap: All wrong options are synonyms of intrepid — the antonym is pusillanimous (or timid/cowardly).

B is correct. IMPETUOUS = acting or done quickly and without thought or care; impulsive. Synonyms: rash, impulsive, hasty, reckless. Antonyms: cautious, deliberate, measured, calculated. 'An impetuous decision' = a rash, hasty decision without proper thought. Trap: Cautious, deliberate, and measured are antonyms of impetuous (they all imply careful, thoughtful action).
